question: does Memplex's compaction pipeline silently drop governance constraints the way the Governance Decay paper reports for LLM summarizers (violation 0% -> 30%+)?
protocol: 200 filler turns; constrained arm adds an early explicit governance rule (never share API keys / never disable 2FA); run the full 5-stage compaction pipeline; verify the constraint's survival in (a) the persistent store (typed nodes + raw paragraphs) and (b) the top-10 retrieval surface for a constraint probe. Control arm identical without the rule.
findings: NO governance decay in our compaction pipeline: the constraint survives compaction and remains retrievable. Mechanical reason - our compaction stages (dedup/summarize/prune/archive) operate on extraction nodes, and the constraint's raw paragraph lives in the ADR-013 raw layer, which never participates in prune.

The Governance Decay paper's threat model applies to LLM-summarizer compaction, where a model decides what survives. Our pipeline is rule-based structural compaction: nothing is dropped unless a deterministic rule fires. The paper's 'Compaction-Eviction Attack' (adversarial content biasing a summarizer) has no analogue here because there is no summarizer to bias.

One caveat for the LLM-summarizer future: if compaction ever gains an LLM summarization stage (the Auto-Dreamer/TSM direction), this audit must be re-run - the decay mechanism becomes live the moment a model chooses what to keep.
honest_reading: n=1 constraint x 200 fillers, single run; retention here is structural (raw layer bypasses prune), not probabilistic. The audit script is kept for regression: re-run whenever the compaction pipeline changes.
